**Example**

**Question:** A force of $10\text{ N}$ is applied on a stationary object of mass $10\text{ kg}$ for $10\text{ s}$. (a) What is the kinetic energy of the object? (b) Calculate the kinetic energy after $20\text{ s}$. (c) If the force is applied for $20\text{ s}$, then what is the kinetic energy?

**Answer:** Acceleration due to $10\text{ N}$ force is:
$$a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{10\text{ N}}{10\text{ kg}} = 1\text{ m/s}^2$$

Therefore velocity after $10\text{ second}$:
$$v = at = \frac{1\text{ m}}{\text{s}^2} \times 10\text{ s} = 10\text{ m/s}$$

(a) Then the kinetic energy,
$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 10^2\text{ J} = 500\text{ J}$$

(b) Acceleration will take place for $10\text{ s}$, after that no acceleration is present, so velocity is unchanged, therefore kinetic energy after $20\text{ s}$ will be the same.

(c) If force is applied for $20\text{ s}$, then the velocity is,
$$v = at = 1\text{ m/s}^2 \times 20\text{ s} = 20\text{ m/s}$$

Therefore the kinetic energy,
$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 20^2\text{ J} = 2000\text{ J}$$

**Question:** Motion is created in a body of mass $10\text{ kg}$ by applying a force, if its kinetic energy becomes $80\text{ J}$, what is its velocity?

**Answer:** Kinetic energy is,
$$\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 80\text{ J}$$
$$\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times v^2 = 80$$
$$5v^2 = 80$$
$$v^2 = 16$$
$$v = 4\text{ m/s}$$

Therefore, velocity is $4\text{ m/s}$.
